holidays.name: National Pizza Party Day
holidays.description: A day to gather your friends, coworkers or classmates and order a pile of pizza boxes. Any excuse works, and the only real rule is that there has to be pizza.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It seems to have grown out of the long tradition of celebrating with pizza at school, the office and birthday parties.
holidays.funFact: Americans eat roughly 100 acres of pizza a day, according to a commonly cited industry estimate. That's a lot of party fuel.

holidays.name: National Mushroom Hunting Day
holidays.description: A day for pulling on your boots, grabbing a basket and wandering into the woods to forage for wild fungi. Foragers treat it as a salute to the thrill of the hunt. You should only eat what an expert has positively identified.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls in mid-May, which is prime morel season in many parts of North America.
holidays.funFact: Morels are famously hard to cultivate commercially. That's why foragers guard their secret patches as closely as buried treasure.

holidays.name: Pack Rat Day
holidays.description: A cheerful nod to people who can't throw anything away, from old receipts and spare cables to boxes of mystery keepsakes. It's a day to embrace your inner hoarder. For the brave, it's also a nudge to finally sort through the clutter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's named after the pack rat, a rodent known for collecting objects.
holidays.funFact: Real pack rats, also called woodrats, build large nests called middens. They fill them with sticks, bones and shiny trinkets, and some middens have lasted thousands of years. Scientists study them for clues about ancient climates.
